The checks below follow the platform published pages in order - what it claims, what the fine print says, and where the two diverge. The verdict is a summary of those checks, nothing more.
whatItClaims: Payouts reportedly within a day.
11 crypto assets through broker partners.
A free demo account with practice funds.
Around-the-clock support through the partner desk.
Signals generated without manual chart reading.
whatWeChecked: The template marks: unfilled placeholders left in the wording.
The performance story: no verified track record behind the return claims.
The number reuse: one score figure doing more than one job.
The deposit terms: minimum amount, payment methods and where the money sits.
The demo claim: practice account confirmed in the signup flow.
The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Fill in the registration form and activate the account via the confirmation email.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Make the US$250 first deposit using any of the listed payment methods.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Configure the risk settings and mode, and keep the demo open while the live account warms up.

pros: Funding by card, transfer, PayPal and Skrill.
cons: One figure doing two different jobs.
redFlags: Ownership details missing from the public pages.
The demo promised in the pitch but buried in the flow.
A score and a community mood wearing the same number.

faqs.a: 11 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: Is Ribera Bitencia safe, legit or a scam?
faqs.a: We found no scam indicators in the product, which reads as a functioning AI trading service. The conditions are editorial: claims without verification, conflicting figures and restriction lists that disagree. We rate it safe to research with the conditions in this review.
US$250, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.

bottomLine: What we found is a real service wrapped in marketing that outruns its own fine print. Trade the service, not the marketing.
The final score lands at 4.5 - a capable platform held back by its own paperwork. Start small, verify the claims yourself and never trade money you cannot lose.
